entries.title: v2026.11.0-beta.3
entries.note: NanoClaw 2026.11.0-beta.3 is the third beta of 2026.11.0: an early test build, so expect rough edges. The November release takes the place of 2026.10.1, which never becomes a stable release; its two release candidates stay published, and everything they brought is in this entry. Installs on the beta channel get this beta; stable stays on 2026.10.0 until 2026.11.0 is published. Since 2026.11.0-beta.1, locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2, /update-nanoclaw no longer stops on a lockfile conflict at the first update of a default

entries.note: NanoClaw 2026.10.1-rc.2 is the second release candidate for 2026.10.1. Installs on the beta channel get this candidate; stable stays on 2026.10.0 until 2026.10.1 is published. entries.title: v2026.10.1-rc.1
entries.note: NanoClaw 2026.10.1-rc.1 is the first release candidate for 2026.10.1. Installs on the beta channel get this candidate; stable stays on 2026.10.0 until 2026.10.1 is published. It lets agents create other agents from templates, adds Cursor as an agent provider, and moves locally built agent images to Claude Code 2.1.296 with Claude Haiku 5.5. entries.title: v2026.10.0
entries.note: NanoClaw 2026.10.0 is the first release with calendar version numbers and the first one /update-nanoclaw installs by default: updates now follow published releases instead of the tip of main . It was tested first as 2026.10.0-rc.1 and 2026.10.0-rc.2 on the beta channel. It also makes updates and rollbacks more dependable, lets Iron Proxy reach a keyless local model over plain HTTP, routes the service through an outbound proxy when you have one, and shows Claude's own reason when a run fails. Iron Proxy installs need one setup rerun, so check the section below before you update. ⚠️ Before you update [BREAKING] OneCLI installs: upgrade the OneCLI gateway to exactly 1.42.0, which closes a credential-injection bypass. /update-nanoclaw never upgrades a running gateway, so this step stops the update until it is done. Follow docs/onecli-upgrades.md in your install ( the same guide on GitHub ):

entries.title: v2.4.0
entries.note: NanoClaw 2.4.0 adds credential gateways installed through skills (OneCLI stays the default, Iron Proxy is new), community-portal setup for Echo's hardened image and a managed Slack app, install-wide and per-group model and speed controls, a Mattermost channel, and a reworked OpenCode provider. Agents now receive all of their capability instructions, replies stay in the thread they answer, and host restarts and /update-nanoclaw are more reliable. The default Claude model moves to Opus 5.5 and new Codex threads to gpt-6-astra , so check the section below before you update. ⚠️ Before you update [BREAKING] Custom source that composes agent instructions must move to the new module. entries.title: v2.3.0
entries.note: [BREAKING] A new Slack experience — per-agent provisioned Slack apps, agent spawning from Slack, and UX improvements — is available to classic single-bot Slack installs. Classic Slack keeps working unchanged; this gate asks for a decision, not a forced migration. New installs and non-Slack installs are unaffected. Migration: run /migrate-slack-agents — it detects classic state (exits cleanly otherwise) and either walks the upgrade or records the choice to stay on classic; both outcomes satisfy this requirement. /add-codex now pins @openai/codex 0.146.0. The previous pin (0.138.0) defaults to GPT-5.4, which OpenAI retires from Codex on 2026-08-31 — codex-provider agents ride the CLI default model, so stock installs stop completing turns at retirement — and it rejects the newer GPT-5.6 models with a 400 asking for a newer Codex CLI.
